title: Large bias-tunable magnetoresistance from spin-dependent interlayer hybridization in van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr-based heterostructures
authors: Sadeed Hameed, Aditya Kumar, Chengjie Yu, Aravind P. Balan, Xinran Wang, Lichuan Zhang, Yuriy Mokrousov, Mathias Kläui
abstract: We explore the large magnetoresistance (MR) in \ce{hBN}/few-layer-graphene/\ce{CrSBr}/few-layer-graphene heterostructures and reveal the mechanism behind its non-monotonic bias dependence. Using bias voltage and temperature as independent tuning knobs, we achieve MR up to \SI{350}{\percent} at \SI{20}{K}, characterized by symmetric M-shaped maxima around $\pm 0.5\,\mathrm{V}$. Continuous tuning of the magnetization angle $θ$ via a hard-axis magnetic field shows that the barrier band-edge offset varies linearly with $\cos(θ/2)$, a first-order signature of spin-dependent interlayer hybridization. This linear relationship rules out the Jullière model and a spin-filter projection. We conclude that the magnetic-configuration-dependent band edge, rather than electrode spin polarization, dictates the large magnetoresistance in \ce{CrSBr} junctions.
summary: This work investigates large magnetoresistance in $	ext{CrSBr}$-based van der Waals heterostructures by measuring transport properties as a function of applied magnetic field angle. The key finding is that the MR mechanism stems from a band edge offset that changes linearly with the cosine of half the magnetization angle, confirming spin-dependent interlayer hybridization rather than simple electrode polarization effects.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate the physical mechanism responsible for large, non-monotonic magnetoresistance (MR) observed in van der Waals antiferromagnetic heterostructures.
main_result: The MR is dictated by a magnetic-configuration-dependent band edge offset, which varies linearly with $\cos(	heta/2)$, ruling out models based solely on electrode spin polarization like the Jullière model.
method: Transport spectroscopy using I-V measurements across varying bias voltages and temperatures, combined with angular dependence analysis of the extracted band-edge offset ($\Phi$).
model_or_system: The system is a $	ext{hBN}/	ext{few-layer-graphene}/	ext{CrSBr}/	ext{few-layer-graphene}$ vertical heterostructure, utilizing $	ext{CrSBr}$ as the magnetic semiconductor.
key_observables: Large MR up to 350% with M-shaped bias dependence; linear variation of band-edge offset ($\Phi$) vs. $\cos(	heta/2$); temperature evolution of transport regimes (VRH vs. activated).
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($20 	ext{ K}$), magnetic field angle ($	heta$), and bias voltage ($V$).
main_assumptions: The transport is dominated by tunneling/hopping limited by the band-edge barrier of $	ext{CrSBr}$.
figures_summary: Figures show I-V sweeps, MR vs. V plots exhibiting M-shapes, and crucial angular dependence plots demonstrating the linear fit of the band-edge offset against $\cos(	heta/2)$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the large MR phenomenon, uses continuous field variation along the hard axis to map the band-edge offset ($\Phi$) as a function of magnetization angle ($	heta$), and analyzes this angular dependence to rule out competing theoretical models.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state magnetism, the precise mapping of energy levels (band edge shifts) based on magnetic configuration provides insights into spin-dependent coupling mechanisms relevant for quantum device engineering.
